title: Voice of customer: adjacent reviews, buyer surveys and thank-you polls
decision_task: Where to source customer language when a business has few or no own reviews, and how mined themes decide what the page says first. / When the business has customers, collect own-customer evidence with a short survey or a one-question post-purchase poll, code it into fixed groups, and map each group to a page section.
applies_when: New business or under ~20 own reviews
Landing page, ad or email brief needs a headline and section order
A category has public reviews of products or services that serve the same outcome
Business has an emailable customer list with consent for service or research messages
Few public reviews but real buyers
A sales page, landing page or onboarding sequence is being written or rewritten
exclusions: The business already has 50+ recent own reviews or survey data (use those first)
Adjacent products serve a clearly different buyer (e.g. luxury vs budget) and language would mislead
The only sources are behind logins or terms that forbid scraping
No lawful basis to contact the list
Fewer than ~10 likely respondents (use 3 to 5 interviews instead)
Survey would be sent from a marketing-only consent that excludes research
required_inputs: Named audience and the outcome they want
The list of what they use today (including DIY or doing nothing)
Owner approval of questions and send
Decision the survey informs (e.g. hook and FAQ for a page)
evidence_requirements: Pool label per snippet: own / competitor / adjacent-outcome
Theme counts as n of N per pool
Raw responses stored privately with respondent count and date
Coding into: problem, feeling, prior attempts, trigger, desired short-term outcome, hesitation/objection, why it mattered
missing_data_behavior: Few own reviews: mine adjacent-outcome reviews as a separate pool, confidence capped at medium.
Fewer than ~10 likely respondents: 3-5 interviews instead of a survey.
No lawful basis to contact customers: public sources only.
alternatives_when_constrained: No reviews: use competitor 2 to 3 star reviews, category forums and adjacent-outcome reviews
No customers yet: same, plus 3 to 5 short episode-based conversations per guide 05
Low traffic: test the mined angle in ads or email first, then move the winner to the page
No reviews: run the survey or poll
No customers yet: episode interviews per guide 05, or CH-C1 mining
Low traffic or tiny list: 3 to 5 phone interviews beat a survey with 4 replies

decision_branches.if: Own customers exist and consent allows research messages
decision_branches.then: Short survey (6-10 questions) or a one-question post-purchase poll, owner-approved.
Label it single-source; themes need frequency.

implementation_steps: Write down audience, desired outcome, current alternatives and where they are discussed before searching
Add an adjacent-outcome pool: reviews of books, tools or services that solve the same problem, kept separate from competitor reviews
Record exact wording into categories (problem, trigger, outcome, objection, proof) without summarising
Rank themes by count and source spread; the top recurring concern goes highest in the message order
Offer 3 to 5 headline candidates from high-confidence phrases (2+ independent sources); a single striking quote is a candidate only, flagged 'single source'
Draft 6 to 10 open questions (not 22) about the last purchase: what was happening, what they tried before, what nearly stopped them, what they expected, what changed
Optional one-question thank-you poll at signup or purchase asking what brought them in today
Code responses into the fixed groups; keep counts and keep raw text
Map: problem and feeling → hook and intro; prior attempts → alternatives and agitation; hesitations → FAQ and the copy near the CTA; triggers → ad and email timing
Report respondent count and response rate honestly; mark non-buyers as missing
dependencies: Owner approval for any survey send

cash_and_labor_requirements.labor: Owner approves questions; ClimbOS codes answers
cash_and_labor_requirements.tools: Survey form; review sources within their terms

metrics: Share of phrase-bank entries with 2+ sources
Downstream: lead-form or booking conversion of the page (not button clicks)
Share of FAQ items traceable to a coded hesitation
Page conversion after rewrite vs before (same traffic source)
guardrails: Never present a mined phrase as a testimonial
Adjacent-outcome evidence is labelled Low/Medium confidence and never blended with own-customer counts
Do not use Google or Amazon search-operator scraping that breaches terms; fetch only what search results return
Never quote a respondent publicly without separate permission
Survey invitation is not a marketing email; keep it free of promotion
Do not quote the reported 87% response rate as an expectation
observation_window: Language bank: refresh every 6 to 12 months or when the offer changes. Page tests: at least two full business cycles (typically 2 to 4 weeks) or until a pre-set conversion count. / Survey open 7 to 14 days; thank-you poll accumulates continuously, reviewed monthly.
stop_conditions: Phrase bank has fewer than 3 themes meeting the finding bar: label thin and propose owner interviews
Adjacent pool dominates (>70% of snippets): flag that language may not fit this buyer
Under 10 responses after 14 days: stop and switch to interviews
Responses dominated by one segment: report as segment-specific
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: skills/voc-research/SKILL.md (source plan, step 3, add adjacent-outcome pool) and skills/landing-pages/SKILL.md step 4 (theme rank informs section order) / skills/voc-research/SKILL.md (new 'own-customer survey' source branch) and skills/landing-pages/SKILL.md step 6 (objections sourced from coded hesitations)

interpretation: LABELLED INTERPRETATION: Copyhackers' main contributions beyond ClimbOS's current skill are the adjacent-outcome source (reviews of things that solve the same problem, not just competitors) and the explicit link from theme frequency to message order. The 400% click case is a single unverified vendor case with a much smaller downstream lift.

LABELLED INTERPRETATION: Copyhackers' survey case used a large, unusually engaged paid list. The transferable part for small businesses is the coding groups and the mapping from groups to page sections, not the length or the response rate.
proposed_climbos_rule: PROPOSED RULE: voc-research adds an 'adjacent-outcome' pool type with its own N and a confidence ceiling of Medium. landing-pages orders problem and objection sections by theme rank from the VOC bank, and states that rank in the brief.

PROPOSED RULE: when own customers exist and consent allows, voc-research offers a short survey or a one-question poll as an owner-approved action. Every FAQ item on a page cites a coded hesitation, a review theme or an owner-confirmed sales objection.
disagreements: Copyhackers lifts one standout quote as the headline. ClimbOS should require frequency or label it single-source. Copyhackers suggests Google site-search operators on Amazon review pages; ClimbOS should not depend on that, given terms and the fetch-only-from-search constraint.

Copyhackers shows a 22-question survey. ClimbOS's brevity rule and small lists favour 6 to 10 questions. Copyhackers found marketer forum comments self-promotional; this supports voc-research's caution on incentivised or performative content.

inputs_hypothetical.business: New mobile dog-grooming van, 4 own reviews
inputs_hypothetical.adjacent: Reviews of dog anxiety books and calming products, 80 snippets

expected_behavior: Creates three separate pools with their own N
Labels the adjacent pool and own pool confidence honestly
Puts the most frequent recurring concern (e.g. a nervous dog) near the top of the page plan with its count
Marks any headline drawn from one quote as single-source
hard_failure: Attributes a book reviewer's words to the groomer's customers
Invents a count or a review

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical
expected_behavior: Proposes a short survey with owner approval, not an automatic send
Maps coded hesitations to FAQ entries with counts
States respondent count and that non-buyers are not represented
hard_failure: Publishes respondent words as named testimonials without permission

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
